abstract: BACKGROUND: Sensory neuropathy (paresthesias), tinnitus, hearing impairment, and Raynaud phenomena are side effects of cisplatin-based chemotherapy used to treat testicular cancer patients. We assessed the long-term occurrence of these side effects among testicular cancer survivors according to the treatment they received. METHODS: A total of 1814 men who were treated for unilateral testicular cancer in Norway during 1980-1994 were invited to participate in a national multicenter follow-up survey conducted during 1998-2002. The men were allocated to six groups according to the treatment they had received. Self-reported symptoms were assessed by a mailed questionnaire that included the Scale for Chemotherapy-Induced Neurotoxicity. A total of 1409 participants who responded to the questionnaire and/or underwent audiometry were assessable in this study. Respondents to the questionnaire (n = 1402) scored the relevant symptoms according to how troubled they were by each (not at all, a little, quite a bit, or very much). Hearing impairment was objectively assessed by audiometry at 4000 Hz in 755 men (seven of whom did not respond to the questionnaire). Group comparisons of symptom assessments were performed with chi2 or Kruskal-Wallis tests. Associations between relevant factors and self-reported symptoms or hearing impairment measured by audiometry were assessed using proportional odds ordinal logistic regression models and linear regression models, respectively. All statistical tests were two-sided. RESULTS: The median follow-up for the 1409 assessable men was 10.7 years (range = 4-21 years). All chemotherapy groups had statistically significantly higher odds for increasing severity of all assessed symptoms and inferior audiometric results compared with men who did not receive chemotherapy. Among chemotherapy-treated men, 39% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 35% to 43%) reported Raynaud-like phenomena (defined as white or cold hands or fingers [or feet or toes] on cold exposure), 29% (95% CI = 25% to 33%) reported paresthesias in the hands or feet, 21% (95% CI = 18% to 25%) reported hearing impairment, and 22% (95% CI = 19% to 26%) reported tinnitus as major symptoms troubling them quite a bit or very much. Hearing impairment (odds ratio [OR] = 5.3, 95% CI = 3.0 to 9.2) and tinnitus (OR = 7.1, 95% CI = 4.1 to 12.4) were particularly common in the dose-intensive chemotherapy group compared with the no chemotherapy group. Men who were treated with radiotherapy had higher odds of self-reported paresthesias in feet compared with those not treated with radiotherapy (OR = 1.5, 95% CI = 1.01 to 2.1, P = .04). CONCLUSION: Long-term survivors of testicular cancer who were treated with cisplatin-based chemotherapy were more often troubled by dose-dependent neurological side effects and Raynaud-like phenomena compared with those who were not treated with chemotherapy.
abstract_ja: 背景：シスプラチン併用化学療法は精巣がん患者の治療に用いられ、感覚神経障害(感覚異常)、耳鳴り、難聴、レイノー現象などの副作用を伴う。われわれは、治療内容に応じた生存者の長期的な副作用発生頻度を評価した。方法：1980〜1994年にノルウェーで片側精巣がんと診断された男性1,814人を招待し、1998〜2002年に全国多施設フォローアップ調査を実施した。男性は受けた治療に応じて6群に分類した。自己申告による症状は、化学療法誘発神経毒性尺度(Scale for Chemotherapy-Induced Neurotoxicity)を含む郵送アンケートで評価した。アンケートに回答し、かつ／または聴力検査を受けた1,409人を評価可能例とした。アンケート回答者(n=1,402)は、各症状がどの程度つらいかを「全くない」「少し」「かなり」「非常に」の4段階で評価した。4000Hzにおける聴力障害は、755人で聴力検査により客観的に評価した(うち7人はアンケートに未回答)。症状評価の群間比較にはカイ二乗検定またはKruskal-Wallis検定を用いた。関連因子と自己申告症状または聴力検査による聴力障害との関連は、比例オッズ順序ロジスティック回帰モデルおよび線形回帰モデルで評価した。統計検定はすべて両側検定とした。結果：評価可能な1,409人の追跡期間中央値は10.7年(範囲4〜21年)であった。すべての化学療法群は、化学療法を受けなかった男性と比較して、全症状の重症度が増すオッズが統計的に有意に高く、聴力検査成績も不良であった。化学療法を受けた男性のうち、39%(95%信頼区間[CI]：35〜43%)がレイノー様現象(寒冷曝露時に手指[または足趾]が白色または冷たくなる状態と定義)を、29%(95%CI：25〜33%)が手足の感覚異常を、21%(95%CI：18〜25%)が聴力障害を、22%(95%CI：19〜26%)が耳鳴りを、それぞれ「かなり」または「非常に」つらい主要症状として報告した。高用量化学療法群では、非化学療法群と比較して、聴力障害(オッズ比[OR]5.3、95%CI：3.0〜9.2)および耳鳴り(OR 7.1、95%CI：4.1〜12.4)が特に多かった。放射線療法を受けた男性は、受けていない男性と比較して、足の感覚異常を自己申告するオッズが高かった(OR 1.5、95%CI：1.01〜2.1、P=.04)。結論：シスプラチン併用化学療法を受けた精巣がんの長期生存者は、化学療法を受けなかった者と比較して、用量依存性の神経学的副作用およびレイノー様現象に悩まされることが多かった。
